rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shira is a verbal noun on the zikra pattern meaning consciousness, and became the name of two first-magnitude stars.
rows.anchor: “Şi‘râ” esasen “zikrâ” vezninde şuur mânasına masdar olup semânın kadr-i evvel kevâkibinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two are Sirius Yaman (Abur) and Sirius Shami (Gumaysa); the unqualified name denotes the brighter Sirius Yaman.
rows.anchor: Şi‘râ-yı Yemânî semânın en parlak yıldızıdır, burada ٱلشِّعْرَىٰ bununla tefsir olunmuştur

rows.speaker: Süddî
rows.claim: Suddī says Himyar and Khuza‘a worshipped Sirius.
rows.anchor: Süddî demiştir ki: “Himyer ve Huzâ‘a ona taparlardı.”

rows.speaker: Âlûsî’nin naklettiği diğerleri
rows.claim: Others cited by Alusi say Abu Kabsha first made Sirius an object of worship; he was from Khuza‘a or its chief Wahz b. Ghalib.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî’nin kaydettiği vechile diğerleri de demiştir ki onu ilk evvel mâbud edinen Ebû Kebşe olmuştu

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify Abu Kabsha as one of the Prophet’s maternal ancestors and explain traits through inherited ancestry.
rows.anchor: Bazıları onu Peygamber’in anası

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others say Abu Kabsha was the kunya of the Prophet’s maternal grandfather Wahb b. Abdimenaf.
rows.anchor: Peygamber’in anası tarafından dedesi Vehb b. Abdimenâf’ın künyesi olduğu

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view identifies Abu Kabsha as the kunya of Halima al-Sa‘diyya’s husband.
rows.anchor: murdi‘ası Halîme-i Sa‘diyye’nin zevcinin künyesi olduğu da söylenmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Arabs revered Sirius, believed it influenced the world, and made occult claims at its rising, naming its Lord shows Sirius is governed, not divine, and its Lord alone should be worshipped.
rows.anchor: Şi‘râ’nın rab değil, merbub olduğu gösterilip o itikadları ibtal edilmiş, Şi‘râ’ya değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ad al-Ula can mean Hud’s people, the old Ad destroyed after Noah; ula distinguishes them from later groups.
rows.anchor: eski Âd kavmini ki Nûh kavminden sonra helâk edilen kavm-i Hûd’dur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı also finds it apparent that ula means the first Ad, contrasted with a later Ad.
rows.anchor: Bazıları “Âd-i Ûlâ” birinci Âd demek olup “Âd-i Uhrâ” mukabili olduğunu söylemişlerdir ki zâhir olan da budur

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Zamakhshari identifies Ad al-Ula as Hud’s people and Ad al-Ukhra as Irem; Elmalılı sees no benefit in the distinction since Irem too was destroyed.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî Âd-i Ûlâ kavm-i Hûd, Âd-i Uhrâ İrem demiştir

rows.speaker: Müberred
rows.claim: Mubarrad identifies Ad al-Ukhra as Thamud.
rows.anchor: Müberred “Âd-i Uhrâ Semûd’dur” demiş

rows.speaker: Taberî
rows.claim: Tabari identifies Ad al-Ukhra as Banu Luqaym b. Huzal, living in Mecca with the Amalika; calling them the mighty ones is similar.
rows.anchor: Taberî “Âd-i Uhrâ Mekke’de Amâlika ile beraber olan Benû Lukaym b. Hüzâl’dir” demiş

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Ad al-Ula were descendants of Ad b. Iram b. Awf b. Sam b. Noah and Ad al-Ukhra their descendants; Elmalılı calls this the closest view.
rows.anchor: Bazıları da “Âd-i Ûlâ, Âd b. İrem b. Avf b. Sâm b. Nûh evladıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı explains the generations through faith: Hud’s unbelieving, stubborn people were destroyed, while a later generation arose in faith; he says this applies to Thamud and others too.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde Âd-i Ûlâ Hazret-i Hûd’a iman etmeyip eski hâllerinde inad ile helâk olanlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud too were destroyed.
rows.anchor: Semûd’u da helâk etti de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma abqa can mean no unbeliever from Ad or Thamud remained, or that no one escaped punishment for their sins.
rows.anchor: hiç bırakmadı yani ne Âd’den ne Semûd’dan iman etmeyenlerin hiçbirini bırakmadı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s people were destroyed earlier and were more unjust and transgressive than the other peoples, greatly tormenting Noah.
rows.anchor: Nûh kavmi öbürlerinden daha zâlim idiler, Hazret-i Nûh’a pek çok ezâ ediyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Ad, Thamud, and Noah’s people were all more unjust and transgressive than Quraysh.
rows.anchor: Âd, Semûd ve daha evvel kavm-i Nûh, hep o helâk edilenler Kureyş’ten daha zâlim ve daha azgın idiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The overturned place refers to Lot’s cities, such as Sodom, cast down into the abyss and beneath the earth; mutafika means turned upside down.
rows.anchor: “Mü’tefike” Lût kavminin altı üstüne gelen şehirleri, Sedum vesâire diye tefsir olunmuştur

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan allows that any town whose dwellings and places were overturned could be intended.
rows.anchor: Herhangi bir inkılab ile mesâkîn ve emâkini alt üst olan her memleket

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated wording magnifies the severity of the punishment that enveloped them.
rows.anchor: bu ifade onlara inen azabı tehvil içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are not celestial disasters unrelated to human action, but calamities resulting from people’s deeds and sins.
rows.anchor: insanların kesb ve zünûblarına terettüb eden felâketleri anlamalıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour, when believers receive reward and disbelievers punishment, draws nearer day by day; people must prepare.
rows.anchor: Sâ‘at yaklaştı mü’minlere sevâbın, kâfirlere ikābın mev‘ud olduğu kıyamet vakti günden güne yaklaşmaktadır

rows.speaker: Ashâb, tâbi‘în ve müteahhirîn müfessirlerinin umûmu
rows.claim: Elmalılı says exegetes across generations agree that the verse reports the splitting-of-the-Moon miracle; the report is famous and transmitted by many Companions.
rows.anchor: mâlum olan müfessirlerin umûmu bunun şakk-ı Kamer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas had not yet been born and Anas was four or five in Medina, but they transmitted the event; Ibn Masud and Jubayr b. Mut‘im witnessed it.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas henüz doğmamıştı, Enes de Medine’de dört beş yaşlarında bulunuyordu

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
rows.claim: Bukhari’s Ibn Masud report has the Moon split into two parts, one above and one below a mountain; the Prophet told them to witness it.
rows.anchor: Buhârî’de İbn Mes‘ûd’dan 1. “Resûlullah’ın devrinde Kamer iki fırkaya inşikak etti; bir fırka dağın fevkinde, bir fırka da dûnunda

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Bukhari’s report from Ibn Abbas says the Moon split during the Prophet’s time.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan: “Peygamber’in zamanında Kamer inşikak etti.”

rows.speaker: Enes
rows.claim: Bukhari reports that Meccans requested a sign and the Prophet showed them the Moon splitting into two parts.
rows.anchor: Enes’ten, “Mekke ahâlisi kendilerine bir âyet gösterilmesini istediler, Peygamber de Kamer’in inşikākını gösterdi”

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
rows.claim: Muslim gives Ibn Masud’s report of two parts, with the mountain between them, and the Prophet’s command to witness.
rows.anchor: Müslim, İbn Mes‘ûd’dan: 1. “Resûlullah’ın ahdinde Kamer iki şıkka inşikak etti, Resûlullah ‘şâhid olun!’ buyurdu.”

rows.speaker: Enes
rows.claim: Muslim reports that Meccans requested a sign and the Prophet showed the Moon split, called merreteyn in one wording and firkateyn in another.
rows.anchor: Enes’ten: “Ehl-i Mekke Resûlullah’tan bir âyet göstermesini istediler, o da ‘merreteyn’ olarak Kamer’in inşikākını gösterdi”

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Muslim’s report from Ibn Abbas is noted as matching Bukhari’s account.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan Buhârî gibi

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
rows.claim: At Mina, Ibn Masud says the Moon split, with one part beyond and one this side of the mountain; the Prophet said to witness and cited this verse.
rows.anchor: Tirmizî, İbn Mes‘ûd’dan: “Biz Resûlullah ile beraber Minâ’da idik Kamer iki filkaya inşikak etti, bir filka dağın ötesinde bir filka da berisinde

rows.speaker: Enes
rows.claim: Tirmidhi’s Anas report says Meccans requested a sign, the Moon split twice in Mecca, and the verses were then revealed.
rows.anchor: Enes’ten: “Ehl-i Mekke Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den bir âyet istediler, binâen‘aleyh Mekke’de

rows.speaker: İbn Ömer
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Moon split during the Prophet’s time and he said, Witness.
rows.anchor: İbn Ömer’den: “Resûlullah’ın ahdinde Kamer yarıldı, Resûlullah ‘şâhid olun!’ buyurdu.”

rows.speaker: Cübeyr b. Mut‘im
rows.claim: Jubayr says the Moon split over two sides of a mountain; some called it magic, while others said magic could not affect everyone.
rows.anchor: Cübeyr b. Mut‘im’den: “Peygamber’in ahdinde Kamer inşikak etti, hatta iki fırka oldu

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: The Shifa report transmitted by Abu Hudhayfa al-Arhabi from Ali says the Moon split while they were with the Messenger.
rows.anchor: Ebû Huzeyfe el-Erhabî rivayetiyle Hazret-i Ali’den: “Kamer inşikak etti, biz Resûlullah ile beraber idik.”

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
rows.claim: In reports through Aswad, Ibn Masud says he saw the mountain between the Moon’s two clefts.
rows.anchor: Esved rivayetiyle İbn Mes‘ûd’dan: “Hatta cebeli, Kamer’in iki fürcesi arasında gördüm.”

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
rows.claim: Through Masruq, Ibn Masud recounts Quraysh accusing Abu Kabsha’s son of magic; another says ask travelers from elsewhere, who confirmed seeing it.
rows.anchor: Mesrûk rivayetiyle İbn Mes‘ûd’dan: “Kureyş kâfirleri ‘Ebî

rows.speaker: Ebû Cehil (Semerkandî’nin nakline göre)
rows.claim: Samarkandi says Abu Jahl called it magic and sent word abroad to ask whether others saw it; they confirmed, but Quraysh still called it lasting magic.
rows.anchor: Semerkandî’nin nakline göre Ebû Cehil “bu bir sihirdir, ehl-i âfâka haber salın gören olmuş mu bakalım” dedi

rows.speaker: Huzeyfe
rows.claim: In a sermon at Mada’in, Hudhayfa says the Hour truly approaches and the Moon truly split during the Prophet’s time; the world announces farewell.
rows.anchor: “Uyanın, Allah teâlâ ٱقْتَرَبَتِ ٱلسَّاعَةُ وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ buyuruyor. Evet Sâ‘at cidden yaklaştı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says these many narrations interpret the verse and, especially in Ibn Masud’s and Ibn Abbas’s wording, establish a past event; Ibn Masud elsewhere lists the Moon among five signs.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı bu bâbda hadis hayli çoktur, bütün bunlar âyetin tefsiri hakkında vârid olmuş rivayetlerdir.

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
rows.claim: Alusi cites reports from several collections that Ibn Masud saw the Moon split into two clefts twice in Mecca before the Prophet’s mission.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî’nin nakline göre Abd b. Humeyd, Hâkim ve İbn Merdûye ve Beyhakī İbn Mes‘ûd’dan dahi

rows.speaker: Irâkī
rows.claim: Iraqi says the occurrence twice is agreed upon and writes that it split twice by consensus.
rows.anchor: Hâfız Ebu’l-Fazl Irâkī Nazmü’s-Sîre’de

rows.speaker: İbn Hacer
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar knows no hadith scholar who asserts repeated occurrences; he says consensus concerns the split, and merreteyn likely means two pieces.
rows.anchor: Hâfız İbn Hacer de bunun hakkında demiştir ki: “Peygamber’in zamanında inşikākın ta‘addüdüne cezmeden ulemâ-yı hadisten kimse bilmiyorum

rows.speaker: İbn İmâm-ı Cevziyye
rows.claim: Ibn Imam Jawziyya explains that marraat can refer to things as well as acts; here it means two pieces, not separate occasions.
rows.anchor: Aliyyü’l-Kārî der ki: “İbn İmâm-ı Cevziyye

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi argues that merreteyn qualifies seeing in Ibn Masud’s report: he saw the split twice, rather than the Moon splitting twice.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî İbn Mes‘ûd rivayetinde şıkkateyn merreteyn denilmiş olması hasebiyle bunun firkateyn mânasına olması yaraşmayacağını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı concludes there was one event; during it the Moon separated and closed twice as rapidly as lightning, with a mountain visible between.
rows.anchor: İnşikāk-ı Kamer vak‘ası iki değil birdir.

rows.speaker: Osman b. Atâ, babasından
rows.claim: Abu Saud cites Uthman b. Ata from his father as saying the Moon will split on Judgment Day; some tafsirs attribute this view to Hasan al-Basri.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud’un nakline göre Osman b. Atâ babasından, سَيـَنْشَ ُّق

rows.speaker: Hasan-ı Basrî
rows.claim: Commentaries such as Nasafi also attribute the future-only reading to Hasan al-Basri.
rows.anchor: Nesefî gibi bazı tefsirlerde bu, Hasan-ı Basrî’ye de atfolunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Quranic past tense can sometimes denote a certain future, Elmalılı rejects that reading here because the next verse describes people seeing a sign and turning away.
rows.anchor: Lâkin burada böyle bir te’vilin mânasız olacağı gösterilmiştir. Çünkü önündeki وَإِن يَرَوْا۟ âyeti bunu reddeyler.

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says all exegetes understand an actual past splitting and reports say the requested sign appeared after the Prophet prayed.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “Müfessirînin hepsi murad

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi calls the future-only reading pointless: a philosopher who denies the miracle rejects it in either tense, while a believer need not reinterpret it.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “Müfessirînin hepsi murad ‘Kamer münşak oldu, onda inşikak vukū‘a geldi’ demek olduğunu söylemişler

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi argues the split is possible and a sound report establishes it; the mutawatir Quran is the strongest proof, making further mass transmission unnecessary.
rows.anchor: Kamer’in yarılması haddizâtında mümkinâttandır, haber-i sâdık ile vukū‘u haber verilince inanmamaya sebep yoktur.

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says absent records by historians or astronomers do not justify denial, nor do claims that celestial bodies cannot rupture and rejoin.
rows.anchor: Hâriçteki müverrihlerin ve müneccimlerin farkına varamamasından veya bir husuf gibi telakkī etmesinden dolayı zabt u kayd etmemiş olmaları vak‘ayı inkâra hak veremeyeceği

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the community agrees against a future-only reading; verse 54:2 refutes it because that statement fits only after the requested sign appeared.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân der ki: وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ kavlinin mânası kıyamette münşak olacaktır

rows.speaker: Huzeyfe
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan cites Hudhayfa’s sermon affirming the Moon truly split in the Prophet’s time; Hasan’s claim of a split after the second trumpet is not to be followed.
rows.anchor: ‘âgâh olunuz ki Sâ‘at yaklaştı ve Peygamberimizin zamanında Kamer hakikaten münşak oldu’

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the claim that moon-splitting means moonrise, with darkness splitting as dawn does.
rows.anchor: “Kamer’in inşikākı, Ay doğduğu esnada zulmetin yarılmasından ibarettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı calls the moonrise metaphor fallacious: although dawn is darkness parting, Moon-rise cannot be called Moon-splitting, and the Quran should be protected from this strained sense.
rows.anchor: Ay’ın doğmasına da “inşikāk-ı Kamer” denilemez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miracle makes the Hour intellectually near by showing the Moon and other celestial bodies can split and collapse; nearness is not just chronological.
rows.anchor: inşikāk-ı Kamer mucizesi Sâ‘at’in zamanda yakınlığından ziyade akla yakınlığını göstermiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Hasan and Ata were misunderstood: they did not deny the past miracle but drew out its indication of a future cosmic split.
rows.anchor: Onlar, Kamer’in kıyamette inşikak edeceğini söylemekle, geçmiş olan inşikāk-ı Kamer vak‘asını inkâr edivermiş gibi farzedilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past split shows celestial bodies may split at the Hour, when Sun and Moon are joined.
rows.anchor: mâzî olan inşikākın müstakbeldeki inşikāka bir delâleti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past event also implies that the Hour and the Prophet’s victory over the polytheists are near.
rows.anchor: Kamer’in inşikākı bir emr-i vâki‘dir, mâzîde vâki‘olan bu inşikak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı places the philosophical debate in kalam; Razi observed that the philosopher denies both past and future splitting.
rows.anchor: Felsefe bakımından meselenin münakaşası ilm-i kelâm meselesidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those unable to conceive miracles, Elmalılı says first direct attention to creation’s wonders, as the Quran often does, then introduces Ibn Sina’s words.
rows.anchor: mu‘cizâtı tasavvur edemeyenlere karşı ilk yapılacak iş Kur’ân’ın birçok yerlerinde yapıldığı vechile hilkatteki acâibâta nazar-ı dikkati celbetmektir
